senses.gloss: סִיגֵּל (Safel of גלל) [to heap up,] to lay by, save; to treasure as a relic.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 9:3:5">Y. B. Bath. IX, 17ᵃ</cite> top <he>בן שנראה חלוק … מה שס׳ ס׳ לעצמו</he> if a son appears to have kept a separate household during his father’s lifetime: what he has saved (of what he took out for his private expenses), he has saved for himself (does not belong to the estate).

<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 1:52">Lam. R. to I, 17</cite> <he>עמד וס׳ וקנה וכ׳</he> he made an effort and economized and bought himself sheep. Tanḥ.Emor, ed. Bub., 30 <he>מְסַגְּלִין עונות וכ׳</he> they accumulate sins during the whole year.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 9">Gen. R. s. 9</cite> <he>כלום … מסגלין … אנו נְסַגֵּל מצות וכ׳</he> the righteous live because they lay by good deeds, we shall likewise lay by good deeds (in order to live).

Koh. R. to I, 3 מְסַגְּלוֹת במצות וכ׳ provide for the future world by means of good deeds; (Lev. R. s. 28, beg. מגדלין במצות heap up; Yalk. Koh. 966 מגדלים מצות; Pesik. Haʿom., p. 69ᵃ מתגדלין, corr. acc.); a. fr.—

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 11:1">Pesik. R. s. 11</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="O00152"><he>סגלה</he></cite>, <cite ref="Exodus 19:5">Ex. XIX, 5</cite>) <he>יכול כמו שהעבד מְסַגֵּל מאחר רבו והבן … והאשה … כך אתם מְסוּגָּלִים לי וכ׳</he> you might think, as a slave lays by something from what his master gives him, or a son from what his father gives him, or a wife from what her husband gives her, so have you been given me as a keepsake: therefore it is written, For mine is the whole earth; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 276:5">Yalk. Ex. 276</cite> <he>כשם שהאשה מְסַגֶּלֶת … כן אתם מסגלין לי מאחורי</he> as a wife …, so could you lay by something for my benefit from what I give you; Mekh. Yithro, Baḥod., s. 2 <he>אף אתם מסוגלין לי מאחרי</he> (corr. acc.).
Sifré Deut. 48 two brothers שהיו מסגלים ממון אחר אביהם that saved what money their father gave them; Yalk. ib. 873.—Part. pass. מְסוּגָּל given as a keepsake, v. supra.
